title: Nut-Free Lemon Blueberry Cupcakes
shortDescription: Light lemon cupcakes with fresh blueberries, ready in 43 minutes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake time.
description: These cupcakes taste like a summer afternoon in a paper wrapper. Fresh blueberries burst inside a soft lemon crumb, and the frosting gets its zip from real lemon zest, not extract. I made these for a backyard party last July and they disappeared before the burgers were done. The batter stays nut-free from start to finish, so they work for school events and shared tables without any swaps. The trick is fresh blueberries only. Frozen ones bleed blue streaks into the batter and turn the crumb gray. A light flour toss keeps the berries from sinking to the bottom. Frosting is simple butter, powdered sugar, and lemon zest whipped until fluffy. It pipes into tall swirls that hold their shape even on a warm day.
ingredients: 1 cup fresh blueberries, plus extra for garnish
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
2 tbsp fresh lemon zest, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl.
Beat 1/2 cup butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in lemon zest and vanilla.
Alternate adding the flour mix and buttermilk with lemon juice, starting and ending with flour.
Toss blueberries with 1 tablespoon flour, then fold gently into the batter by hand.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
Beat 1 cup butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar in two batches.
Mix in lemon zest and heavy cream, then whip 2 minutes until light and fluffy.
Pipe frosting onto fully cooled cupcakes and top with a fresh blueberry.
tips: Pat blueberries dry with a paper towel before tossing in flour so the coating sticks.
Use room temperature eggs and butter so the batter blends smoothly.
Chill piped cupcakes 10 minutes before serving outdoors so the frosting holds its shape.
Zest lemons before juicing them. It is much easier that way.

faq.question: Can I use frozen blueberries instead of fresh?
faq.answer: Fresh blueberries work best for this recipe. Frozen berries release extra liquid and turn the batter gray and streaky as they bake.

faq.question: Why did my blueberries sink to the bottom of the cupcake?
faq.answer: This happens when berries are not coated in flour first. Toss them lightly in a tablespoon of flour before folding into the batter.

faq.question: Can I make the frosting less sweet?
faq.answer: Yes, cut the powdered sugar to 3 cups and add an extra pinch of salt. The lemon zest will still come through clearly.

faq.question: How far ahead can I bake these cupcakes?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in an airtight container. Frost the day you plan to serve them.

conclusion: These lemon blueberry cupcakes bring a light, summery taste to any table. Fresh berries and real lemon zest make them worth the short prep time.
